featured_reviews.name: Chaitra Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text:
Underwent a laser piles procedure at Galaxy Hospital, Mira Road, and what followed was one of the worst healthcare experiences I’ve had.

The nursing staff appeared poorly trained, inattentive, and completely lacking in basic patient care protocols. During my discharge, I was given a potassium permanganate sitz bath where an entire packet was used instead of the medically appropriate small pinch concentration. I experienced severe burning and later discovered chemical burns across my buttocks, which have now left visible scarring on both sides — something deeply unpleasant, with long-term impact that, at this point, does not seem like it will go away.

What is even more shocking is that despite:

- me informing the nurse that a full packet had been used,
- complaining of burning sensation twice before discharge,
- and undergoing surgery just a day prior,

not a single doctor physically examined my surgical wound before discharging me.

Post-surgery, I had also complained about excessive discharge from the wound to the extent that bedding had to be changed, yet no doctor came to assess me then either.

After raising the matter formally with the hospital in extensive detail, not once did anyone ask me to return for examination of the burns or assess the injury they now claim did not exist. Instead, every response took 3–4 days and consisted largely of denying responsibility, dismissing my experience, and attempting to shift the blame onto the patient.

If a hospital’s idea of patient safety is expecting post-surgery patients — while medicated and without medical expertise — to diagnose their own chemical burns, that says everything about their standards of care.

Extremely disappointing experience. I would strongly caution anyone considering treatment here.
